clue.text: A difficult walk I had, that's clear

parts.note: to limp is to walk with difficulty, as with an injured leg
'd is the contracted form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Someone admits an awkward hobble was obvious to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' reads naturally as I'D, which is exactly what the wordplay wants: I plus D.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water or prose is transparent and easy to see through, a synonym for clear.

clue.text: Take no notice of developing region

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of region are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disregard an area that is still being built up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay it no attention.

clue.text: Plant tree with land round

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree
to bag is to land or catch, as game or a prize
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fruit tree with a patch of ground around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' is a verb here, to catch, not ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a flowering shrub, also called leadwort, so a kind of plant.

clue.text: Consignment of French uniform

parts.note: de is the French word for of
livery is the distinctive uniform of servants or a company

explanation.surface: A shipment of French military kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery is a batch of goods sent or handed over, a consignment.

clue.text: Something used in the lists by many a knight

parts.note: the lists were the jousting arena, where knights charged with a long spear
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A jousting weapon described as carried by plenty of knights in the tournament field.
explanation.walkthrough: The lists here are the enclosed ground for medieval jousting, not written lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the famous Round Table champion in Arthurian legend, a specific example of a knight.

clue.text: Still wearing former outfit, the first one had

indicators.note: wearing means the word for former has the next word on it, i.e. around it

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
yet means still, as in yet more

explanation.surface: Someone still in their old clothes, the first ones they owned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a baby's first set of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothing and linen prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Find most of country's heath frighteningly cold

indicators.note: most of means the country's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Chile is a South American country
ling is heather, the plant of the heath

explanation.surface: Locate the moorland of a nation that is scarily icy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilling describes something cold enough, or scary enough, to make one shiver.

clue.text: Learned to repeat first line

indicators.note: first places the line's letter at the start, before the word for repeat

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: A scholar has to recite the opening line again.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means well read or educated, i.e. learned.

clue.text: At sea, weed two tars used to keep afloat

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and there are two of them
the second of the two sailors

explanation.surface: Two sailors at sea use seaweed to stay buoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had 'cars', an OCR slip; the page prints 'tars'. Mix WEED with TAR twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is to stay upright in water by moving the legs, keeping afloat.

clue.text: Girl friend embraces you finally — at regular intervals

indicators.note: embraces means the pair holds another letter between them

parts.note: Ann is a common girl's name
an ally is a friend or supporter

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A girlfriend finally hugs you, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done each year happens at regular yearly intervals, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: During match turn over a new leaf and tread very carefully

indicators.note: During means the second piece sits within the first, in the middle of the match

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie
PTO, please turn over, is printed at the foot of a page to tell the reader to go to the next leaf

explanation.surface: A player reforms in mid-game and starts moving cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over a new leaf' looks like the idiom for reforming, but it is the page instruction PTO; a cup TIE is a British term for a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: To move on the tips of the toes is to walk very quietly and cautiously.

clue.text: Well fitted to reform idolater

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suit cut to measure for a worshipper of idols who has mended his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes made to measure by a cutter fit their wearer well.

clue.text: New books, after ten years, deteriorating

indicators.note: after places the books behind the ten-year period in the word

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NT, the New Testament, is the collection of new books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Fresh books, a decade on, are falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes something in moral or cultural decline, i.e. going downhill.

clue.text: Event for cars setting off up a road originally

definitions.text: Event for cars setting off up a road originally

parts.words: Event for cars setting off up a road originally
parts.note: a contest in which cars set off together from a standing start on a straight stretch of road, which was originally an ordinary street

explanation.surface: A motoring contest where cars set off from a standing start along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor sport in which cars accelerate from a standstill over a short straight course is this event.

clue.text: Boy meeting maiden — all for nothing, perhaps?

parts.note: Antony is a boy's name
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A lad meets a girl and gives up everything for nothing, as in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: 'all' and 'nothing' are opposite words, so 'all' is an example of one for 'nothing'. M for maiden comes from cricket scoring, where a maiden is an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning to another, as all is to nothing, is that word's opposite term.

clue.text: Without saying much, whip up island to revolution

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for whip is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the cat, the cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
a turn is one revolution

explanation.surface: Someone tight-lipped stirs an island into rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests revolt but means one full rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means habitually silent or reserved in speech.

clue.text: Race in public

definitions.meaning: the Grand ... is the famous British steeplechase run at Aintree, often just called the ...
public as in belonging to the whole country, as in the public debt

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National horse race is commonly shortened; and state-wide, as opposed to private, things are of the whole nation.

clue.text: Invention produced by US agents in sudden burst of activity

indicators.note: in places the agents inside the burst of activity

parts.note: a fit is a sudden spell of activity, as in fits and starts
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: A new device turned out by American federal agents in a frantic rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid's PIGMENT is a misprint: the wordplay and the definition give FIGMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something made up, a product of the imagination.

clue.text: I blacken Dominican, for instance

parts.note: to blacken someone's name is to slander them

explanation.surface: A man confesses to smearing a Dominican friar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dominican' suggests the religious order, but it means a native of the island of Dominica.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Dominica, a Caribbean island nation, is an island dweller.

clue.text: Convert so solemn and dark

indicators.note: convert means change into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solemn and gloomy religious convert.
explanation.definitionFit: A night with no moon visible is dark.

clue.text: First of 2 1 old records I left on

parts.note: EPs, extended plays, are old vinyl records

explanation.surface: The opening track of a list is on some old records someone abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 1' is the clue number 21 down: its answer begins with E, and this is the Greek name for that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's equivalent of E is called by this name, so it stands for the opening letter of the other light.

clue.text: Jumper has to go to side of track

definitions.meaning: a jumper is a knitted top pulled on over the head
to ... is to steer a vehicle to the edge of the road

explanation.definitionFit: A knitted sweater is a garment pulled over the head; drivers also pull to the roadside and stop.

clue.text: I have found so-called stockade

definitions.meaning: Archimedes' cry of discovery in Greek
the stockade at Ballarat, Australia, scene of the 1854 miners' rebellion, bore this name

explanation.walkthrough: The stockade is the Australian goldfields rebellion of 1854, known by the name of the local diggings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek exclamation translates as 'I have found it'; the 1854 Australian gold miners' fort carries the same name.

clue.text: They have a belief that's strange — saintism

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the next word are made odd, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Believers in a cult call it peculiar saint-worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the doctrine that natural objects have souls hold a religious belief.

clue.text: Lizard — one relocated in South American region

indicators.note: relocated means one letter is taken up and set down at a new spot in the region's name

parts.note: Guiana is the region on the north-east coast of South America
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lizard, a single one, moved into a part of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift the I in GUIANA to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

clue.text: After entry of snake, went ahead and ran

indicators.note: entry of means the snake goes into the word for went ahead

parts.note: led means went in front
the adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: After a snake came in, someone took the lead and fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' is the stocking sense: a ladder is a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights that have laddered have run, developing a vertical line of broken stitches.

clue.text: Nerve centre of criminal organisation discovered by hero

parts.note: a gang is an organised band of criminals
a lion is a brave or celebrated person, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: The headquarters of a crime syndicate is uncovered by a courageous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a mass of nerve cells acting as a relay point in the nervous system.

clue.text: Something of a whippersnapper, a scallywag

definitions.text: Something of a whippersnapper, a scallywag

indicators.note: something of means only a part of the following words is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A cheeky young upstart is a bit of a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the last of 'whippersnapper' through 'a' into 'scallywag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous rogue, like a cheeky youngster or a scamp.
